shortDefinition: AI systems that can understand, reason about, and generate content across multiple types of data including text, images, audio, and video.
fullDefinition: Multimodal AI refers to models that can process and generate multiple types of data — text, images, audio, and video — within a single system. Unlike earlier AI models that handled only one modality, multimodal models can relate concepts across different forms of data. For example, a multimodal model can analyze an image and describe it in text, generate an image from a text description, or transcribe and translate spoken audio. This cross-modal understanding enables more natural and versatile AI applications, from accessible tools for visually impaired users to rich creative platforms. Models like GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude 3 Sonnet are leading examples of multimodal AI.
examples: Describing the contents of a photo and answering questions about it
Generating an image from a detailed text description
Transcribing a meeting recording and creating a text summary with action items
